newsitem.title: USA: Clinton picks Shelton for top U.S. military officer.
newsitem.headline: Clinton picks Shelton for top U.S. military officer.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has chosen Army Gen. Henry Shelton to be the next chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff, U.S. officials said on Wednesday.
The officials, who asked not to be named, said Clinton was expected to announce the nomination of Shelton to become the top U.S. military officer on Thursday.
Shelton, a 34-year veteran who commanded the U.S. military operation in Haiti three years ago, now heads the U.S. Special Operations Command, an elite group of 47,000 Army, Navy and Air Force troops.

The officials said Defence Secretary William Cohen on Wednesday formally recommended that Shelton replace Army Gen. John Shalikashvili as chairman of the Joint Chiefs and came with him to the White House for an interview with Clinton.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry declined comment late on Wednesday on whether Clinton had selected Shelton. Earlier in the day he noted Clinton knew the officer well because of his role in the Haiti operation.
Finding a replacement for Shalikashvili, scheduled to step down at the end of September, has proved troublesome for the administration.

Cohen's first choice, Air Force Gen. Joseph Ralston, withdrew from consideration in June after the disclosure of an adulterous affair more than 10 years ago when he was separated from his wife. Ralston is vice chairman of the joint chiefs.
After Ralston withdrew, Cohen interviewed a number of other four-star candidates from all military services and said last week that he had narrowed the field to three or four.

Others reported to be on that list included Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Charles Krulak; Navy Adm. Joseph Lopez, chief of southern NATO forces based in Naples, Italy; and Army Gen. Wesley Clark, recently named head of all allied NATO forces in Europe.

If approved by the Senate, Shelton would jump from leading 2 percent of U.S. forces to running the whole show from the Pentagon. That 2 percent, however, includes some of the most rugged members of the U.S. armed forces, including the Army's Green Berets, Navy Seals, and Air Force special tactics and para-rescue personnel.
A tall, square-jawed Army Ranger, Shelton does not stand on formality and goes by his middle name, Hugh.

Shelton, a native of Tarboro, North Carolina, did not attend the elite U.S. Military Academy at West Point. He has a textile engineering degree from North Carolina State University and a master's degree from Auburn University in Alabama.
